create_media_systems.ponder.jukebox.head: Streaming Custom Discs
create_media_systems.ponder.jukebox.text: Use a Custom Disc in the air to write a YouTube or Discord link onto it. The server checks that the link plays before writing it.
In any jukebox it streams to everyone nearby: loud up close, fading out with distance.
To limit who hears it, right-click the jukebox with a Jukebox Range Quill to pick it.
Then select two corners like with the Schematic and Quill, and right-click again to set the volume. Only players inside the range hear it.
Right-click the picked jukebox again without a selection to change just the volume, or reset the range.
create_media_systems.ponder.speakers.tex: A Disc Reader plays a Custom Disc without making a sound itself...
...for the Speakers linked to it. Speakers also work with a jukebox, playing in sync with it.
With the Range Quill, pick the source, then right-click each speaker to link it and set its volume and channel.
Set one to Left and one to Right for stereo, or leave them on Mix.
Turn a speaker with a Wrench. It is loudest in front and quiet behind.
create_media_systems.ponder.train_disc_r: An Announcement Schedule is edited like a Train Schedule: add a station, then announcements for the trip there, each with its own link: on departure, after N seconds, at N%% of the way, N seconds before arrival, or on arrival.
Put it in a Train Disc Reader on the carriage. It can be swapped even after the train is assembled.
Train Speakers on the same train play it, without linking. Each is heard only in its own carriage.
To set their volume, hold right-click on the reader with a Wrench while the train is disassembled.
When the train departs for or arrives at a matching station, the announcement plays, fading in and out as riders get on and off. Several readers play at once.
Play at N% of the way
create_media_systems.screen.channel: Channel (detectors and receivers with the same name are linked)
create_media_systems.ponder.train_detect: Place a Train Detector like a Train Observer: right-click the track first, then place it nearby.
Give the detector and a Train Signal Receiver the same channel (empty hand). Receivers can be anywhere.
While a train is over the detector, every receiver on its channel gives a redstone signal of 15. Distance and unloaded chunks don't matter.

create_media_systems.ponder.equalizer.te: An Equalizer touching a Blu-ray Player turns the Low, Mid and Hi of its sound up or down, on its displays and speakers alike.
Point at a fader, hold right-click and look along it: the knob follows, showing you its gain, and everyone hears it once you let go. Each goes up or down by up to 12 dB.
A second Equalizer touching the first splits each band in two and takes the lower half: BASS, Low-Mid and Hi-Mid. More than two do nothing.
Sneak to place a block on its top instead. Through Engineer's Goggles it shows each band's gain.
create_media_systems.ponder.blu_ray_play: DVDs, Blu-rays and the Blu-ray Player
Use a DVD or a Blu-ray in the air to write its playlist, one video link per row, or a YouTube playlist link to fill it with the playlist's videos. The server checks every link before writing them.
A DVD holds 16 videos played at up to 480p, and a Blu-ray 64 at up to 1080p. Neither plays in a jukebox.
Right-click a Blu-ray Player with either disc to play its videos one after another; it stops after the last. Right-click with an empty hand to take the disc out.

Its volume is set like any Create value: hold right-click on its top with a Wrench. It turns its displays and its speakers up or down alike. Its front sets how brightly its displays light their surroundings, the same for everyone; 0% turns it off.
Shift+right-click it with a Remote to pair them. Use the Remote in the air for its buttons: previous, play/pause, stop, next, play a video by number, and volume.
A Remote reaches its Blu-ray Player only within the server's range (64 blocks unless set otherwise).
Through Engineer's Goggles it shows which video it plays, and how loud.
create_media_systems.ponder.display.head: Displays
create_media_systems.ponder.display.text: A Display goes on the side of a wall, where it shows a Blu-ray Player's video.
Hold a Display Quill, right-click a Blu-ray Player to pick it, then right-click displays to link them; again to unlink. Any number of displays can show one player.
Looking at a display with the quill, Ctrl+scroll makes it a block wider or narrower (a sixteenth with Shift). It grows right and up, and its height follows its ratio.
Shift+right-click steps through the ratios: free, 16:9, 4:3, 21:9, 1:1, and the video's own. Alt+scroll sets the height alone.
Its sound comes from the middle of the picture, at the player's volume. While a speaker plays that Blu-ray Player, only the speakers are heard.

create_media_systems.ponder.image_viewer: An Image Viewer goes on the side of a wall like a Display, and shows a picture from a link.
Right-click it with a Wrench to type the image's link: a PNG, JPEG, GIF (its first frame) or BMP, from a site the server allows. Each player's game downloads it.
Size it with a Display Quill, just like a display. Shift+right-click's last ratio is the image's own.
Right-click it with the quill to take its frame away: only the picture is left, and the wall shows through where the image is transparent. Right-click again to put the frame back.
Through Engineer's Goggles it shows its link and size.
create_media_systems.ponder.lighting_con: A Lighting Console is 4 desks wide and 2 deep, all facing the same way, with a Lighting Console Monitor on each desk of the back row. It comes together as soon as the last block is in place.
Point at its controls with an empty hand or a Wrench: right-click buttons and pads, scroll over a value to change it, and hold right-click to move a fader or the aim pad.
Its faders set each of the six groups' brightness and the master. The rest, on the desk and the monitors, set the selected group's colours, presets, motion, aim, and how it follows sound and video.
Through Engineer's Goggles it shows the selected group and how many fixtures are linked.
create_media_systems.ponder.stage_lights: Stage Lights and the LED Tuning Wrench
Moving Head Lights, Strip Lights and Laser Projectors light up the stage. A Lighting Console drives up to 64 of them, in six groups.
Hold a LED Tuning Wrench and right-click a finished console to pick it.
Then right-click fixtures to link them to the group selected on the console. Right-click one again, or Shift+right-click it, to unlink it.

Right-click a Blu-ray Player, a Disc Reader or a jukebox to link it too. Turn on sound or video linking on the console, and the lights follow its music or its picture's colours. Shift+right-click a Blu-ray Player to link only its picture.
Looking at a fixture with an empty hand, scroll to move it to another group. Shift+scroll changes its place in the group's order, and Ctrl+scroll the colour it takes from the group.
Right-click a player with the LED Tuning Wrench to have the selected group follow them, or Shift+right-click the air to be followed yourself.
Place a fixture under a ceiling to hang it upside down. Through Engineer's Goggles it shows its group and order.

create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_1: A hi-fi stack is separate units in one block: place one, then use the next on it. A whole set of five fills the block. Any order works, and any unit can be left out.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_2: Sneak and right-click it with an empty hand to take the top unit off again.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_3: Every unit but the amplifier needs its flat cable: use an Audio Cable on the socket at its back. The disc player needs its line cable too, or it plays unheard. Right-click a plug to pull it out.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_4: For sound, use an Audio Cable on one of the amplifier's speaker terminals, then on a hi-fi speaker: one for the left, one for the right. Sneak and right-click a speaker with an empty hand to pull its cable out.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_5: Point at a button and right-click to press it. Hold right-click on a knob and look left or right to turn it. What you point at is named above the hotbar.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_6: Open the disc player's tray and put a CD, DVD, Blu-ray or Custom Disc on it. A DVD or Blu-ray also shows on displays linked to the stack with a Display Quill.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_7: Put a Cassette Tape in either deck. A tape remembers where it was stopped, so rewind it to hear it from the top.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_8: The amplifier picks what is heard and how loud. The sound controller shapes it with its presets and shows its spectrum. A Remote paired with the stack works its disc player and volume from afar.

create_media_systems.keyboard.midi.none: No MIDI device (click to look again)
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.ba: BANK ◄: the previous of the 16 pad banks.
BANK ►: the next of the 16 pad banks.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.sn: SNAP SHOT: recall one of 8 stored panel settings. Press it, a pad, then NEXT. With SHIFT lit, stores the current settings on that pad instead.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.pr: PREV (EXIT): leaves snapshot mode without doing anything.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.ne: NEXT (ENTER): recalls or stores the snapshot on the pad picked.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.pr: PROG CHG: the pads pick the sound of the framed zone. 16 banks of 8 cover all 128 General MIDI sounds.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.cc: CC: the pads switch controllers on and off for the framed zone. Bank 1: damper, sostenuto, soft, modulation, reverb, chorus.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.sh: SHIFT: click to light it, then: UPPER 1 turns the arpeggiator on or off, OCT -/+ picks the velocity curve, SPLIT lets the next key set the split point, SNAP SHOT stores.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.fu: FUNC: click to light it, then press the key under one of the functions it shows above the keys.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.kn: R1 CUTOFF: how bright the framed zone sounds. Drag up and down, or scroll.
R2 RESONANCE of the framed zone's filter.
R3 ATTACK: how slowly the framed zone's notes come in.
R4 RELEASE: how long the framed zone's notes ring after a key is let go.
R5 REVERB of the framed zone.
R6 CHORUS of the framed zone.
R7 PAN: the framed zone to the left or right speaker.
R8 VOLUME of the framed zone.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.lo: LOWER zone and its sound: click to turn it on and frame it for the pads and knobs; click the framed zone again to turn it off. Zones that are on play layered.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.up: UPPER 1 zone and its sound: click to turn it on and frame it for the pads and knobs; click the framed zone again to turn it off. With SHIFT lit: the arpeggiator.
UPPER 2 zone and its sound: click to turn it on and frame it for the pads and knobs; click the framed zone again to turn it off.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.sp: SPLIT: LOWER plays the keys up to the split point, the UPPER zones those above. With SHIFT lit, the next key pressed becomes the split point.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.tr: TRANSPOSE: click to light it, then OCT -/+ shift the keys by semitones (-6 to +5).
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.s1: S1: sends controller 80 while held. With the arpeggiator on: HOLD.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.s2: S2: sends controller 81 while held. With the arpeggiator on: TAP TEMPO.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.oc: OCTAVE -: an octave down (to -4). With TRANSPOSE lit a semitone down, with SHIFT lit a lighter velocity curve.
OCTAVE +: an octave up (to +5). With TRANSPOSE lit a semitone up, with SHIFT lit a heavier velocity curve.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.le: Pitch bend / modulation lever: drag left and right to bend, push it away to add vibrato.
create_media_systems.ponder.midi_keyboar: The keyboard is three blocks wide in one block: set it on a desk with room to either side. Right-click it to sit down and play. One player plays it at a time, until they close the screen.

Its keys, pads, knobs and buttons are worked with the mouse. The computer's keyboard plays it too: the rows from Z and from Q are its keys, Space its damper pedal. A real MIDI keyboard plugged into the computer plays it as well.
It sounds from itself. To play it through speakers, pick it with a Range Quill, then right-click each speaker: set one to the left channel and one to the right.
Everyone nearby hears and sees what is played, as it is played. The pads pick the sound: 128 of them, in 16 banks of 8.
Here is a piano piece played on it.
create_media_systems.ponder.px_s1100.tex: Feed Forge Energy into the rear of the bass side, or use a charged battery.
Connect a MIDI keyboard to your computer. Select the device in Settings.
Right-click to play with the mouse, computer keyboard, or MIDI. Space works the damper.
Pick the piano with the Jukebox Range Quill, then right-click each Speaker to link it.
Set Left and Right for stereo. Use Mix for one speaker. Linked speakers take over the sound.
